description.summary: web views hosted by a media centre compositor

protocol.description:
This protocol lets a compositor that hosts a web browser as one of its clients drive the browser's views and learn their state, so that the compositor can present a page as part of its own user interface: open a URL on the user's behalf, navigate, show the title and favicon, offer bookmarks, and hand input to the page while it is in front.
The compositor spawns the browser itself and the browser connects over an inherited socket. The browser is the Wayland client: requests are what the browser tells the compositor, events are what the compositor asks of the browser.
Views are grouped by profile. A profile names a hermetic set of cookies, storage and credentials kept by the browser; views of different profiles never share them. The compositor decides which profile a URL opens in and what that profile looks like to the web: user agent, user scripts and content filters are configured per view before the first page loads, as file descriptors the browser reads.
Content filters use the Adblock Plus filter syntax, the format maintained ad and tracker lists such as EasyList are published in, so that one list serves any engine. The browser applies the filters its engine can express and ignores the others.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is experimental and backward incompatible changes may be made. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes are done by bumping the version number in the protocol and interface names and resetting the interface version.

interface.name: kodi_web_manager_v1

description.summary: create and announce web views

interface.description:
The global through which the browser announces itself and creates views. A browser binds it once.
The compositor asks for a view of a profile with the want_view event; the browser answers with a create_view request for that profile and creates no view on its own. One view per profile: a second create_view for a profile the compositor already knows is a protocol error. The browser keeps running without views.
A profile identifier is 1 to 255 bytes of ASCII letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', other than "." and "..", compared case-sensitively. The browser may use it verbatim as a file name. The profile "default" keeps nothing across runs; the compositor opens pages that belong to no other profile in it.

entry.name: duplicate_profile
entry.summary: a view for this profile already exists

entry.name: invalid_surface
entry.summary: the surface already belongs to another view

entry.name: invalid_profile
entry.summary: the profile identifier is not valid

request.name: destroy

description.summary: destroy the manager

request.description: Destroy the manager. Existing views are unaffected.

request.name: create_view

description.summary: create a view for a profile

request.description:
Create a view that renders into the given surface and associate the view with it. The browser makes the surface an xdg_toplevel through xdg_wm_base as usual; the compositor configures it fullscreen at its own resolution.
The profile names the hermetic storage this view uses. The compositor configures the view with set_user_agent, add_user_script, add_content_filter and add_content_filter_list events before its first load_url, so the browser loads nothing into a fresh view on its own.

arg.name: surface
arg.summary: the surface the view renders into

request.name: ready

description.summary: the browser is ready to serve views

request.description: Sent once the browser is connected and can create and load views. The compositor shows no web entry point as available before it.

event.name: want_view

description.summary: the compositor wants a view for a profile

event.description:
The compositor needs a view for the given profile and none exists. The browser answers with create_view for that profile. If it cannot, or the profile identifier is not valid, it answers with a view_unavailable request.
The uplink names the local source address every connection of the profile's view is bound to, so that a host with more than one uplink can choose the one a profile leaves through. It is an IPv4 address, an IPv4 subnet such as 192.168.5.0/24, or an interface name; a subnet or an interface name is resolved for every new connection, so it survives a new DHCP lease. A connection whose uplink does not resolve fails rather than leaving through another uplink. An empty string leaves the connections to the system's routing. A browser that cannot bind connections answers a non-empty uplink with view_unavailable.

arg.name: uplink
arg.summary: source address, subnet or interface, or empty

request.name: view_unavailable

description.summary: a wanted view cannot be created

request.description: The browser cannot create the view asked for by want_view, for example because the profile's storage is unusable.

event.name: content_filter_list

description.summary: a shared content filter list

event.description:
A content filter list the compositor keeps for every view, such as a maintained ad or tracker list, in Adblock Plus filter syntax as UTF-8 text. The compositor sends every list it holds after the browser binds the manager, and a list again whenever its content changes; a list sent under a name the browser already has replaces it. Views apply a list once they ask for it with add_content_filter_list.
The browser prepares the list at once, independently of any view, and reports the outcome with content_filter_list_prepared. A list the browser cannot prepare leaves the version it prepared before in place. The fd holds exactly size bytes; the browser closes it.

arg.name: name
arg.summary: list identifier, same syntax as a profile identifier

event.name: remove_content_filter_list

description.summary: a shared content filter list is gone

event.description: The compositor no longer keeps the named list. Views that applied it drop it.

request.name: content_filter_list_prepared

description.summary: a shared content filter list is prepared

request.description: The browser has prepared the list of this name a content_filter_list event handed it, so that views can apply it, or it could not and holds no earlier version of the list (prepared 0). A list the browser kept prepared from an earlier run is reported as prepared as soon as it is handed again.

arg.name: prepared
arg.summary: 1 if views can apply the list, 0 if not

entry.name: left_to_right
entry.summary: the language is written left to right

entry.name: right_to_left
entry.summary: the language is written right to left

event.name: layout_direction

description.summary: the direction of the user's language

event.description: The direction in which the language of the user's session is written, independent of any page's content. Pages of a book in that language turn forward in this direction, so a swipe in from the edge where the language starts goes back in a view's history and a swipe in from the other edge goes forward. The compositor sends it after the browser binds the manager and again whenever the language changes.

interface.name: kodi_web_view_v1

description.summary: one web view of one profile

interface.description:
A view is one page container bound to one surface. The compositor drives it with events and learns its state through requests.
Configuration events (set_user_agent, set_viewport, add_user_script, add_content_filter, add_content_filter_list) apply to this view only and take effect from the next navigation. They arrive before the first load_url of a view the compositor asked for, and the browser holds that load until it has applied them. A shared list the browser does not have yet, or has not finished preparing, does not hold the load; it applies once it is there.
An inactive view keeps its page alive: media keeps playing and scripts keep running, so that the user can leave the page and come back to it. The browser may lower an inactive view's rendering frequency. The compositor stops a view's media by loading about:blank, and discards a view with the close event.

enum.name: error_code

description.summary: what went wrong with a view

enum.description: Reported by the error request. The message carries the engine's own text for the log; the code is what the compositor acts on.

entry.name: load_failed
entry.summary: the page could not be loaded

entry.name: tls_failed
entry.summary: the TLS handshake or certificate check failed

entry.name: engine_crashed
entry.summary: the engine process rendering this view terminated

entry.name: config_failed
entry.summary: a user script or content filter could not be applied

request.name: destroy

description.summary: destroy the view

request.description: The browser is done with the view. Sent in answer to the close event, or on its own when the view can no longer be served, after an error request. The association with the surface ends; the browser destroys the surface or its role object afterwards.

request.name: url_changed

description.summary: the view's URL changed

request.description: Sent whenever the committed URL of the view changes, including fragment navigation within the page.

request.name: title_changed

description.summary: the page title changed

request.description: Sent whenever the document title changes. An empty string means the page has no title.

request.name: favicon

description.summary: the page favicon is available

request.description: Hands the compositor the page's favicon as an ARGB8888 wl_shm buffer. The compositor copies what it needs and releases the buffer with wl_buffer.release; the browser destroys it after the release. A view sends a new favicon request whenever the icon changes.

request.name: load_progress

description.summary: load progress of the current page

request.description: Progress of the current load in percent, 0 at the start of a navigation and 100 when the load finished.

request.name: navigation_state

description.summary: history availability changed

request.description: Whether the view can go back or forward in its history.

request.name: error

description.summary: the view failed

request.description:
Something went wrong with the view. After engine_crashed the browser either recovers the view, in which case it follows up with url_changed, or destroys it.
After config_failed the browser loads nothing into the view; a later load_url fails the same way. The message names the script or filter.

request.name: exit

description.summary: the page asks to leave

request.description: The page asks to leave the app and return to the compositor's own interface, for example from its Quit menu entry. The compositor decides what follows, usually closing the view. Sent at most once per load_url.

request.name: media_state

description.summary: what the page's media is doing

request.description: Whether the media of the view's current page has video, has audio, and is paused. paused is 1 unless some media of the view is potentially playing; buffering counts as playing. A page without media reports video 0, audio 0, paused 1. Sent when any of the three changes, and after each committed load.

event.name: set_user_agent

description.summary: set the user agent of this view

event.description: The user agent string this view presents. Takes effect from the next navigation. A view configured without it uses the browser's default.

event.name: add_user_script

description.summary: inject a user script into this view

event.description: A script the browser injects into every document of this view at document start, in the main world, before any page script runs. The script is read from the file descriptor, which holds exactly size bytes and which the browser closes; fewer bytes is config_failed. Scripts apply in the order they are added.

event.name: add_content_filter

description.summary: apply a content filter to this view

event.description:
Filters the browser applies to every load of this view, in Adblock Plus filter syntax as UTF-8 text. The fd holds exactly size bytes; the browser closes it. A filter sent again under the same name replaces the earlier one.
A filter that cannot be read in full, is not UTF-8, holds no filter the engine can apply, or holds more than the engine accepts, is config_failed.

event.name: add_content_filter_list

description.summary: apply a shared content filter list to this view

event.description: Apply the shared list of this name, as sent by the content_filter_list event of the manager. The view loads nothing before the list is prepared: load_url waits for a list that is not there yet, and a list that cannot be prepared, with no earlier version to keep, or that is removed before it is, is config_failed. A list replaced later is applied to this view once it is prepared; a list that is removed is removed from the view.

event.name: load_url

description.summary: load a URL

event.description: Navigate the view to the URL. about:blank unloads the page and stops its media.

event.name: navigate

description.summary: history and load control

event.description: Go back or forward, reload, or stop the current load.

event.name: set_active

description.summary: the view is shown or hidden

event.description: Active means the compositor presents the view's surface and routes input to it. An inactive view keeps running and may render less often; it must still commit a frame when its content changes, so that the compositor has a current picture when it activates the view again.

event.name: close

description.summary: the compositor is done with the view

event.description: The browser unloads the page, unmaps the surface and destroys the view. The profile's storage stays.

event.name: set_viewport

description.summary: the viewport the page lays itself out for

event.description: The size in CSS pixels of the viewport the view's pages are written for, such as the 1920x1080 of a television's browser. The browser zooms the page so that a viewport of this size fits the view, keeping its aspect ratio, and follows changes of the view's size. Where the view is wider or taller in proportion, the page gets the remainder. Takes effect at once. A view configured without it, or with a width or height of 0, lays out at the size of its surface.
